description:
Hypothesis: install sigaction for SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGILL/SIGFPE around kernel execution; a fault whose PC is inside a loaded defk .so -> siglongjmp to the NIF boundary, release ctx->owned, raise RuntimeError for the calling process; PC anywhere else -> restore the previous handler and re-raise (node dies as today).

Must answer:
1. ERTS coexistence: OTP explicitly permits NIF-local signal use during a call if restored before returning (PR #7174); ERTS uses SA_ONSTACK alternate stacks on scheduler threads, so our handler must set SA_ONSTACK too and save/restore the previous sigaction (chain if it was not SIG_DFL).
2. Install scope: per-call install/restore (matches the documented contract; a window where unrelated faults are not contained is loss-only) vs per-library-load with PC gating. sigaction is process-wide; synchronous faults are delivered to the faulting thread.
3. Post-fault soundness: kernels never touch the BEAM heap mid-compute (only off-heap binaries in ctx->owned; terms are made at return), so if the PC is in kernel compute code, raise-for-caller is heap-sound; PC inside enif_*/libc -> re-raise. Residual: a wild write that never faults cannot be contained - document, do not hide.
4. Prototype + tests: test-only kernel with a deliberate null deref at a controlled point, run in a :peer node - caller gets the exception, node survives, other processes keep running; a fault outside kernel ranges still kills the node (we do not mask unrelated crashes).

Scope: POSIX first, Windows as a documented limitation. Reuse the :peer crash-test harness pattern from defk-63k.

Done when: feasibility note + accept/reject decision recorded on this ticket, prototype tests pass in a peer node if accepted. Findings feed docs/beam-nifs.md section 5 and the runtime-contract section of defk-sgw.5.

comments.text: Docs target: findings feed docs/beam-nifs.md section 5, ticket defk-7w2 (placeholder section until this spike decides).

Fault containment becomes load-bearing with the from-scratch decoders in defk-52v (lz4/snappy defk-52v.3, inflate/PNG defk-52v.7, zstd defk-52v.8, JPEG defk-52v.12): they parse attacker-controlled bytes, and the safety claim in each ticket is 'raises, never crashes the VM'. The fuzz-agreement runs in those tickets are the evidence this ticket needs.

Alternative to weigh (not yet considered in the repo): run a kernel outside the VM instead of containing faults inside it. OTP's erl_interface (ei, OTP 29.1.1, https://www.erlang.org/doc/apps/erl_interface/ei_users_guide.html) is the C library for port programs and C nodes: it encodes and decodes the external term format (ei_x_*) and lets a C program act as a distributed node (ei_connect, ei_send/ei_receive, ei_rpc). Defk-generated C linked into a port program or C node would give real OS-process isolation: a fault or a wild write that never faults kills only that process, which signal-based containment cannot cover (see point 3's residual). Cost: every call copies its arguments and result through the external term format and makes an OS process round trip; ei is only guaranteed compatible within one OTP release unless ei_set_compat_rel() is used. Inside a NIF ei is the wrong tool, because enif_* already works on the live terms. Inference, not measured: for small high-rate calls (about 12 ns per scalar kernel call today, defk-25s) the round trip likely erases the win; for the defk-52v decoders on large attacker-controlled inputs it might not. Worth one measurement (port round trip vs NIF call across input sizes) before the accept/reject decision, so the verdict can say when to choose a port backend over signal containment.

Feasibility note and decision (2026-10-13, branch defk-7dm/fault-containment): ACCEPT, built, tests pass. ADR-0009 (docs/adr/0009-fault-containment.md) records it.

1. ERTS coexistence: per-library handler for SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGILL/SIGFPE, installed at load and upgrade with SA_SIGINFO | SA_ONSTACK | SA_NODEFER (the guard's sigsetjmp(jb, 0) saves no mask, so SA_NODEFER keeps the signal unblocked after the longjmp); previous sigaction saved and chained (SA_SIGINFO handler, plain handler, or the default action put back so the fault re-executes and kills the node as before).

2. Install scope: per library image at load, not per call (sigaction is a syscall; per call would cost ~1 us against a 12 ns call). The running call is a thread-local set by the generated guard function (one lookup per call: 12.5-12.7 ns -> 12.7-13.2 ns per scalar call; two lookups cost 2.5 ns, since __thread in a dylib on macOS arm64 is a call per access). PC gating: the library's own __TEXT segment (macOS, getsegmentdata) or executable PT_LOAD (Linux, dl_iterate_phdr), PC from the ucontext (arm64 and x86-64). The chain reaches every library's handler, so a fault in an older library passes the newer handlers (each checks its own range) before its own contains it. An image never leaves a dangling handler: at unload it restores the previous handler if its own is the head, else pins itself (dlopen RTLD_NOLOAD | RTLD_NODELETE); at upgrade the new image pins the old one via the priv_data ERTS hands over (ERTS never calls an upgraded image's unload; its suspended kernels run until the purge). Finding: on macOS dyld never unmaps an image with thread-local storage, so purged kernel libraries now stay mapped there regardless (verified with vmmap: main unmaps, the branch keeps it mapped even with the pin disabled); Linux unmaps unless pinned, which the chain test covers only on Linux (defk-a1p). Windows: documented limitation.

3. Soundness: contained only when si_code > 0 (synchronous), a kernel of this library runs on the thread, and the PC is inside the library's code. Kernel code holds no lock and touches no BEAM heap mid-compute, so the longjmp to the guard is exactly a raise: owned buffers released, RuntimeError 'defk bug: <signal> inside kernel native code (signal, code, address, pc +offset); the call was aborted and the node kept running'. Not contained, by design: faults in ERTS or libc called from a kernel (memcpy, libm, enif_*: a longjmp out of an allocator or a lock would corrupt it), in another NIF, in the library outside a call, a wild write that never faults, a corrupted C stack (SIGABRT from libc). Documented in runtime-contract.md, language.md section 9, beam-nifs.md section 5, scope.md (the 'Not yet' bullet is gone), CONTEXT.md ('Contained fault').

4. Tests: test/fault_containment_test.exs (9 tests). __defk_inject_fault__/1 (test-only hook like __defk_corrupt_tags__/1, compiled in under DEFK_FAULT_HOOKS = MIX_ENV=test) faults at a clock read: segv (address 8), illegal instruction (udf/ud2), integer division by zero (x86-64 only), after N clock reads (so also inside a promoted frame, the step function path). In the VM: the caller gets the RuntimeError, the hook is consumed, the library works again, frames_live returns, a concurrent kernel of another library in another process is unaffected, the raise is on the calling process only. In a child VM (mix run under MIX_ENV=test): a fault in libc called from a kernel kills the node, a fault in the library outside a call kills the node, and the chain holds across a hot upgrade (K2 then K; upgrade K; purge; fault in K2 contained through new K and old K) and across unloads (U1 non-head, U2 head). Removing the pin did not fail the chain test on macOS (dyld keeps TLS images mapped), so that path is covered by construction here and needs a Linux run.

5. The alternative (ei / port program): measured, bench/port_roundtrip.exs, performance.md 7.10. Floor: 7.8 us per call at 8 B (600x a kernel call), 28/38 us at 64 KB (ack/echo), 263/402 us at 1 MB, 4.4/7.3 ms at 16 MB (2.5-4 GB/s one way). It pays only for long, coarse calls (argon2 20-90 ms: yes; lz4/snappy decode 0.04-0.18 ms: the pipe costs 1-5x the work; scalar kernels: no). Kept as a deployment choice named in the verdict, not defk's boundary.

Residual for the verdict's Limitations: wild writes without a fault, faults inside libc/ERTS, Windows, Linux unverified for the pin path (defk-a1p).

title: Fault containment: turn a kernel fault into an exception for the calling process
